cards.text: In the tenth year, on the twelfth day of the tenth month, the word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel the prophet. God calls him "Son of man" and hands him a new assignment. He's to set his face against Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and prophesy against him and against all Egypt.
Ezekiel's to tell Pharaoh that the Lord GOD is against him. God calls him a great monster who lies among his rivers.

cards.question: The great monster lying among his rivers has a brag about the Nile. What does Pharaoh say?

answers.text: The Nile is mine and I made it myself
The Nile was handed to me by my gods
The Nile will flow forever just for me

cards.text: God says He'll put hooks in Pharaoh's jaws and haul him up out of his rivers.

cards.question: As God hauls the river monster up out of his rivers, what comes up clinging to his scales?

cards.text: God says He'll leave him in the desert with all the fish of his streams, to fall on the open field.

cards.question: After the river monster falls on the open field, he'll be gathered up for a proper burial.
God says He's given Pharaoh as food to the beasts and the birds. When that happens, what will all the people of Egypt know?

answers.text: That their gods have left them
That their king has run away

cards.text: Then God brings up the house of Israel, and how they'd been leaning on Egypt. He has a picture for what Egypt was to them: a staff.

cards.question: God says Egypt was only a staff of ___ to the house of Israel.
When Israel takes hold of Egypt, that staff of reeds, what happens?

answers.text: It splinters and tears their shoulders
It holds but bends down low
It sinks into the soft mud

cards.text: And when they leaned on it, it broke, and their backs were wrenched. That's the cheap office chair at work, friend: lean back ONE time and you're having a meeting with the CEILING.

cards.question: Because of all this, God says He will bring a sword against Egypt and cut off man and beast.

cards.text: God says, "The land of Egypt will become a desolate wasteland. Then they will know that I am the LORD."
Then God brings up Pharaoh's words again, "The Nile is mine; I made it," and says that's why He's against him.

cards.question: Because of that Nile brag, God says He is against Pharaoh and against his ___.

cards.text: So God says He'll turn the land of Egypt into a ruin, a desolate wasteland from Migdol to Syene, and as far as the border of Cush.

cards.question: Once Egypt is a ruin from Migdol to Syene, what does God say about anyone passing through the land?

answers.text: No man or beast will pass through

cards.question: God says Egypt will be uninhabited for forty years. During that time, the Egyptians stay together in their own land.

cards.text: But God's not done talking about Egypt. He looks ahead to the end of those forty years.

cards.question: When the forty years are up, what does God say He'll do with the scattered Egyptians?

answers.text: Gather them back from the nations

cards.text: God says He'll restore Egypt from captivity and bring them back to the land of Pathros, the land of their origin. Home again, after forty years away.

cards.question: Back in Pathros, God says Egypt will be a ___ kingdom.
Someday Egypt will rise up again and rule over the nations.

cards.text: Then God says what this lowly Egypt will mean for the house of Israel, the ones who leaned on that staff of reeds. Friend, after that office chair, I'd be done leaning too.

cards.question: God says Egypt will never again be something Israel puts its trust in. Instead, what will Egypt remind the house of Israel of?

answers.text: Their sin in turning to Egypt
Their years as slaves in Egypt
Their escape across the Red Sea

cards.text: That's the end of the first message. Then the date jumps to the twenty-seventh year, on the first day of the first month, and the word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel again.

God tells him Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, worked his army hard against Tyre, and every head was made bald and every shoulder made raw. Baker, that's the kind of overtime where you clock out and your shoulders file a COMPLAINT.

cards.question: After all that hard labor against Tyre, Nebuchadnezzar and his army got paid well by Tyre.

cards.text: So the Lord GOD has something in mind for Nebuchadnezzar.

cards.question: God says He will give the land of ___ to Nebuchadnezzar, and its plunder will be the ___ for his army.
Why does God say He gives Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar as the reward for his labor?

answers.text: Because the labor was done for God
Because Babylon begged God for it

cards.text: Then, at the very end, God says that in that day He'll cause a horn to sprout for the house of Israel.

cards.question: God also says He will open Ezekiel's mouth to speak among the house of Israel.

cards.text: And God closes with that line one more time: "Then they will know that I am the LORD." Pharaoh said he made the Nile, but the last word here belongs to the LORD.
